doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Goodman's photographs claim, and Bucky Pizzarelli as his favourite
summary: Goodman wanted money from any photos Appleyard took; years later Goodman's photo sold at auction. They wonder why Goodman favoured Bucky Pizzarelli.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Well he operated on his own terms, didn’t he, to be generous or to be the typical Benny.

Once he said to me, “Why do you take so many pictures?” I have a Leica you see, and I took a lot of pictures. I said, “Why, does it bother you, Benny?” He said, “If you ever take any of me and sell them, let me know.” He wanted the money. So anyway, a couple of years ago I was in this second-hand shop this friend of mine used to run. And he had a tradepaper. “Oh,” he said, “It was at an auction of musicians’ artifacts in New York by Southeby’s.” He said, “This stuff of Benny Goodman’s.” “This hat,” and he showed me a picture of it and I knew what it was because I recognized the hat, and a pair of shoe trees, and a photograph of Benny and his daughter sold for $1,750. I had taken the photograph.

So I looked to him and I said, “Benny, finally, I didn’t get the money, somebody got $1,750 for the photographs. I had taken it in Copenhagen when we were there, we took it at Tivoli Gardens. Yeah. Bucky was with us quite a lot. Bucky was one of his favorites.
Yeah. Why would a musician be his favorite? Were you able to figure that out?

I really don’t know. Bucky had a very nice personality and his wife is very lovely. I don’t know. Because the one European tour that we did, Bucky was on guitar, he never gave him one solo the whole tour.
